easy.def: A small bag sewn into clothes.
examples: I put it in my pocket.
My pants have two pockets.
Keep your hands in your pocket.

more.def: A small bag sewn into clothing for holding small things.
examples: She keeps a tissue in her pocket.
His coat has deep pockets.
I found a coin in my jeans pocket.

related.def: As much as a pocket can hold.

easy.def: A long case that holds seeds.
examples: Peas grow in a pod.
The pod is green.
The pod is full of seeds.

more.def: A long case on a plant such as a pea or bean that holds the seeds.
examples: Peas grow inside a green pod.
The bean pod split open.
The pods dry up in autumn.

easy.def: A short piece of writing in lines.
examples: I wrote a poem.
The poem rhymes.
Mom read me a poem.

more.def: A piece of writing that uses lines, rhythm and often rhyme to share feelings or ideas.
examples: I wrote a poem about my cat.
The poem has four lines that rhyme.
She read a poem about the moon.

easy.def: A person who writes poems.
examples: The poet read a poem.
A poet wrote this.
She is a poet.

more.def: A person who writes poems.
examples: The poet read her poem to the class.
The poet wrote about the sea.
My uncle is a poet.

easy.def: Poems.
examples: I like poetry.
We read poetry in class.
The book is full of poetry.

more.def: Poems as a kind of writing, with lines that often rhyme and share feelings in a special way.
examples: We read poetry every Friday in class.
She writes poetry about nature.
The book is full of poetry about the sea.

easy.def: A sharp end.
examples: The pencil has a point.
Do not touch the point.
The star has five points.

more.def: The sharp, thin end of something.
examples: The point of the needle is very sharp.
The pencil broke at the point.
A star has five points.

easy.def: One score in a game.
examples: We got a point.
She scored a point.
The game is tied by a point.

more.def: A unit used to keep score in a game or contest.
examples: Our team scored three points before the break.
You get one point for every right answer.
She won the game by two points.

easy.def: To show where something is with your finger.
examples: I point at the bird.
She pointed to the door.
Point to the moon.

more.def: To show where something is by holding out a finger or an object toward it.
examples: The guide pointed to the top of the cliff.
She pointed at the map to show where we were.
The arrow points north.

easy.def: Something that can make you very sick.
examples: Poison is dangerous.
Some mushrooms are poison.
The bottle said poison.

more.def: A substance that can make a person or animal very sick or kill it.
examples: Some snakes have poison in their fangs.
The label warns that the cleaner is poison.
Some wild mushrooms are poison.

easy.def: To push something with a finger or stick.
examples: I poke the dirt with a stick.
She poked the cat's nose.
He poked a hole.

more.def: To push something quickly with your finger or a pointed thing.
examples: I poked the dirt with a stick.
She poked a hole in the paper with her pencil.
The turtle poked its head out of its shell.

easy.def: A long, thin stick.
examples: The tent has a pole.
A flag is on a pole.
He held the pole.

more.def: A long, thin piece of wood or metal, usually standing up.
examples: The flag hung from a tall pole.
He held a fishing pole.
The tent stood up on two poles.

easy.def: One end of the earth, far north or far south.
examples: The North Pole is cold.
Penguins live near the South Pole.
The pole is covered in ice.

more.def: The very top or the very bottom of the earth, which are covered in ice.
examples: The North Pole is covered with snow and ice.
The compass needle points toward the North Pole.
Explorers traveled to the pole by dog sled.

easy.def: People whose job is to keep a town safe.
examples: The police helped us.
Call the police.
A police car drove by.

more.def: A group of people whose job is to keep the public safe and to make sure laws are followed.
examples: The police helped the lost boy find his parents.
A police officer stopped the traffic so the children could cross.
The police station is next to the library.

easy.def: A man who works for the police.
examples: The policeman helped us cross.
A policeman is at the corner.
The policeman wore a badge.

more.def: A man who works for the police, keeping people and places safe.
examples: The policeman helped us cross the street.
A policeman directed the traffic.
The policeman gave directions to the lost tourist.

easy.def: A rule or plan.
examples: The school has a policy.
The policy is no phones.
It is our policy.

more.def: A set of rules or plans that people agree to follow.
examples: The school has a policy about running in the halls.
The store has a return policy.
It is our policy to share.

easy.def: To rub something to make it shiny.
examples: I polish my shoes.
She polished the table.
He polished the silver.

more.def: To rub something until it is smooth and shiny.
examples: I polished my shoes until they shone.
Dad polished the car on Sunday.
She polished the silver spoons.

easy.def: Something you rub on to make things shiny.
examples: I used shoe polish.
The polish is shiny.
The wood polish smells nice.

more.def: A cream or liquid that you rub on something to make it shiny.
examples: Dad rubbed polish on his boots.
The furniture polish smelled like lemons.
She painted her nails with red polish.

easy.def: Having good manners.
examples: It is polite to say "thank you."
The polite girl said "please."
Be polite to the bus driver.

more.def: Having good manners and showing respect for other people.
examples: The polite boy held the door open for everyone.
It is polite to wait until everyone is served before eating.
He wrote a polite letter to thank his aunt.

easy.def: With good manners.
examples: She asked politely.
He thanked me politely.
They waited politely.

more.def: In a way that shows good manners.
examples: She asked politely for a glass of water.
He thanked the host politely.
The children waited politely in line.

easy.def: Having to do with the government and how a country is run.
examples: Voting is a political act.
The mayor is a political leader.
We learned about political parties.

more.def: Having to do with government, leaders and the way a country or city is run.
examples: The class learned about political leaders in our country.
A political party chooses people to run in the election.
The mayor gave a political speech.

easy.def: A person who works in government.
examples: The politician gave a speech.
A politician visited the school.
The politician shook hands.

more.def: A person who is in a job in government or who runs for one.
examples: The politician gave a speech to the town.
A politician visited our school to talk about voting.
The politicians met in the capital.

easy.def: The work of running a country or town.
examples: Politics is about government.
My uncle works in politics.
She is interested in politics.

more.def: The activities of choosing leaders and making the rules for a place.
examples: My aunt works in politics.
The class talked about politics and voting.
The mayor has been in politics for ten years.

easy.def: Dirty things that hurt the air, water, or land.
examples: Smoke from cars makes pollution.
Pollution makes the air dirty.
We pick up trash to stop pollution.

more.def: Harmful or dirty things that spoil the air, water, or land.
examples: Pollution in the river made it unsafe for the fish.
Factories must work to cut down on pollution.
Noise pollution from the airport bothers the neighbors.

easy.def: A small lake.
examples: The ducks swim in the pond.
The pond is cold.
A frog sat by the pond.

more.def: A small body of still water, smaller than a lake.
examples: Ducks swam on the pond.
A frog croaked by the pond.
The pond froze over in winter.

easy.def: A small horse.
examples: I rode a pony.
The pony is brown.
The pony has a short mane.

more.def: A kind of small horse.
examples: The children took turns riding the pony.
A pony is smaller than a horse.
The pony trotted around the ring.

easy.def: A place filled with water for swimming.
examples: We swim in the pool.
The pool is cool.
Kids splash in the pool.

more.def: A large tank of water for swimming.
examples: We swam in the community pool.
The pool is deep at one end.
She learned to dive at the pool.

easy.def: A small puddle or pond.
examples: A pool of water.
Frogs sit by the pool.
There is a pool of rain.

more.def: A small area of water that has collected in one place.
examples: After the storm, a pool of water stayed on the road.
Frogs gathered by the shallow pool.
Starfish live in rock pools by the sea.

easy.def: Having very little money.
examples: The poor family needed food.
They were poor, but happy.
The poor village had one school.

more.def: Having little money or few things.
examples: Long ago, a poor farmer found a magic bean.
Some poor families get help buying food.
The poor town had one old school.

easy.def: Used when you feel sorry for someone.
examples: Poor kitten, you are wet!
Poor baby is tired.
The poor bird hurt its wing.

more.def: Used to show that you feel sorry for someone.
examples: The poor puppy is shivering in the rain.
Poor Max had to stay home with a cold.
The poor kitten was stuck in the tree.

easy.def: Not good.
examples: His writing is poor.
The poor light made it hard to read.
Poor weather ruined the picnic.

more.def: Of low quality or not good enough.
examples: The sound in the old theater was poor.
She got a poor grade because she did not study.
A poor harvest meant less food for the winter.

easy.def: To burst with a short sound.
examples: The balloon popped.
Corn pops in the pan.
Bubbles pop.

more.def: To burst or break open with a quick, short sound.
examples: The balloon popped and made me jump.
Popcorn kernels pop when they get hot.
I heard the soap bubbles pop.

easy.def: A short loud sound.
examples: I heard a pop.
The balloon went pop.
A pop came from the fire.

more.def: A short, sharp sound like a small burst.
examples: The cork came out with a loud pop.
We heard a pop from the fireplace.
The balloon burst with a pop.

easy.def: Corn that puffs up when it is heated.
examples: I eat popcorn at the movies.
The popcorn is hot.
We made popcorn.

more.def: A snack made from corn kernels that burst open and puff up when heated.
examples: We ate popcorn at the movies.
The popcorn popped in the pan.
I put butter on my popcorn.

easy.def: The leader of the Catholic Church.
examples: The Pope lives in Rome.
The pope gave a speech.
The people waved at the pope.

more.def: The leader of the Catholic Church, who lives in Rome.
examples: The pope lives in a small country inside Rome.
Crowds gathered to see the pope.
The pope spoke to people from many countries.

easy.def: Liked by lots of people.
examples: Soccer is a popular game.
This is a popular book.
Pizza is popular with kids.

more.def: Liked or enjoyed by many people.
examples: That song is so popular that everyone knows the words.
The beach is popular with tourists in summer.
She is popular because she is friendly to everyone.

easy.def: The number of people in a place.
examples: The town has a small population.
The population is big.
The population grows.

more.def: The total number of people or animals that live in a place.
examples: The town has a population of five hundred.
The city's population has grown.
The population of the whales is rising.

easy.def: A covered area at the front of a house.
examples: We sat on the porch.
The porch has a swing.
The cat is on the porch.

more.def: A covered area built onto the front or back of a house.
examples: We sat on the porch and watched the rain.
The porch had a swing.
The mail was left on the front porch.

easy.def: Meat from a pig.
examples: We had pork for dinner.
The pork is cooked.
I like pork chops.

more.def: The meat of a pig, eaten as food.
examples: We had roast pork for dinner.
The pork was tender.
She served pork with rice.

easy.def: A place by the water where ships stop.
examples: The ship is in port.
The port is busy.
We saw ships at the port.

more.def: A town or harbor where ships come to load and unload goods.
examples: The ship stayed in port for two days.
Cranes unloaded boxes at the busy port.
We visited a port on the coast.

easy.def: A grand door or gate.
examples: The portal to the castle was huge.
We passed through the portal.
The portal is stone.

more.def: A large, impressive door or entrance.
examples: The stone portal of the castle was huge.
We passed through the portal into the hall.
A magic portal appeared in the story.

easy.def: A part of something.
examples: I ate a small portion.
A portion of the cake.
The portion is big.

more.def: A part or share of a whole thing, or an amount of food for one person.
examples: I ate a small portion of the pie.
A portion of the money went to charity.
The portions at the restaurant were big.

easy.def: A picture of a person.
examples: The portrait hangs on the wall.
She painted a portrait.
The portrait is of my mom.

more.def: A painting, drawing or photograph of a person.
examples: A portrait of the queen hung on the wall.
The artist painted a portrait of her mother.
The school takes a class portrait.

easy.def: To hold your body still, for a picture.
examples: We pose for a photo.
She posed for the painter.
The cat posed by the window.

more.def: To hold a position so that someone can take a picture or draw you.
examples: The family posed for a photo.
She posed for the painter in a blue dress.
The cat posed by the window like a statue.

easy.def: The way you hold your body.
examples: She struck a pose.
The yoga pose is hard.
The dancer held a pose.

more.def: A position that you hold your body in.
examples: The dancer held a graceful pose.
She struck a silly pose for the camera.
Tree pose is a yoga position.

easy.def: The place or way something is.
examples: Stay in your position.
Put the ball in position.
I changed my sitting position.

more.def: The place where something is, or the way it is placed.
examples: The players ran to their positions on the field.
Sit in a comfortable position.
Check the position of the hands on the clock.

easy.def: A job.
examples: She has a new position.
He applied for a position at the zoo.
The school has a position open.

more.def: A job in a company or group.
examples: She applied for a position at the library.
He holds an important position at the bank.
The school has a position open for a cook.

related.def: To move something to a new position.

easy.def: Hopeful and happy.
examples: She has a positive attitude.
Be positive.
He is positive.

more.def: Thinking about the good side of things.
examples: She has a positive attitude about school.
A positive person looks for the bright side.
He felt positive about the test.

easy.def: Sure.
examples: I am positive.
He is positive he locked it.
She was positive about the answer.

more.def: Completely sure about something.
examples: I am positive that I locked the door.
He was positive about the answer.
She was positive the bus was late.

easy.def: To own or have.
examples: She possesses a rare coin.
I possess a key.
He possesses great strength.

more.def: To own or have something.
examples: The old castle possesses a hidden room.
The museum possesses a very old map.
The family possesses land by the river.

easy.def: Something that you own.
examples: This book is my possession.
He packed his possessions.
Her favorite possession is a doll.

more.def: Something that belongs to you.
examples: This bike is my favorite possession.
He packed all his possessions into a box.
The family lost most of its possessions in the flood.

easy.def: Something that may happen.
examples: There is a possibility of rain.
A snow day is a possibility.
Winning is a possibility.

more.def: A thing that might happen or might be true.
examples: There is a possibility that the game will be canceled.
Scientists studied the possibility of life on other planets.
We talked about every possibility before choosing a name.

easy.def: Able to happen.
examples: It is possible to fly.
Is it possible to go?
Rain is possible.

more.def: Able to happen, be done or be true.
examples: It is possible to see the stars from here on a clear night.
Is it possible to finish before lunch?
Snow is possible tomorrow, but it may rain instead.

easy.def: Maybe.
examples: It may possibly rain.
Could you possibly help?
He possibly forgot.

more.def: It could be, but it is not certain.
examples: It may possibly snow tonight.
Could you possibly lend me a pencil?
She is possibly the fastest runner in school.

easy.def: A tall piece of wood or metal in the ground.
examples: The fence post is tall.
A post holds the sign.
The horse is tied to the post.

more.def: A strong, upright piece of wood or metal set in the ground.
examples: Dad nailed the sign to a post.
The horse was tied to a fence post.
A tall post held up the porch roof.

easy.def: To put up a sign or message.
examples: Post the sign.
She posted a picture.
He posted a note.

more.def: To put up a notice or message where people can see it.
examples: The teacher posted the schedule on the door.
She posted a photo on the class page.
He posted a sign by the gate.

easy.def: To send a letter.
examples: Post the letter.
I posted a card.
He posts letters.

more.def: To send something by mail.
examples: Mom posted the letter on the way to work.
I posted a card to my cousin.
He posts packages on Fridays.

easy.def: A card with a picture that you mail.
examples: I got a postcard.
The postcard has a beach.
She sent a postcard.

more.def: A card with a picture on one side that is sent through the mail without an envelope.
examples: I got a postcard from my aunt.
The postcard showed a beach.
She sent us a postcard from Paris.

easy.def: A big picture or sign on a wall.
examples: I hung a poster.
The poster is of a tiger.
The poster is on my wall.

more.def: A large printed picture or notice that is put on a wall.
examples: I hung a poster of a tiger on my wall.
A poster at school told about the fair.
The movie poster was bright and colorful.

easy.def: To put off until later.
examples: We postponed the game.
The picnic was postponed.
They postponed the trip.

more.def: To move something to a later time.
examples: We postponed the game because of rain.
The picnic was postponed until Saturday.
They postponed the trip for a week.

easy.def: A deep round dish for cooking.
examples: Mom cooked soup in a big pot.
The pot is hot.
Put the pasta in the pot.

more.def: A deep, round container used for cooking or for holding plants.
examples: The soup simmered in a big pot on the stove.
She planted a seed in a small clay pot.
He stirred the pot of chili with a wooden spoon.

easy.def: A round vegetable that grows in the ground.
examples: I eat a baked potato.
Potatoes grow underground.
Mom mashed the potato.

more.def: A round vegetable with brown skin that grows under the ground.
examples: Dad baked a potato for dinner.
Potatoes grow underground, and farmers dig them up.
She made French fries from a potato.

easy.def: What someone could become.
examples: She has potential.
He has great potential as a swimmer.
The potential is there.

more.def: The ability to grow, develop or become something in the future.
examples: The coach saw great potential in the young player.
The seed has the potential to become a tall tree.
She has the potential to be a good writer.

easy.def: A magic drink in a story.
examples: The witch made a potion.
The potion was green.
She drank the potion.

more.def: A liquid in stories that is said to have magic powers.
examples: The witch stirred a bubbling potion.
In the story, a potion made him invisible.
The wizard mixed a potion in a cauldron.

easy.def: A way to measure how heavy something is.
examples: The baby weighs ten pounds.
I bought a pound of apples.
A pound of flour is heavy.

more.def: A unit for measuring weight, equal to 16 ounces.
examples: The baby weighed eight pounds.
We bought a pound of apples.
The bag of flour weighs five pounds.

easy.def: To hit again and again.
examples: Rain pounded on the roof.
He pounded the drum.
Waves pound the shore.

more.def: To hit something hard many times.
examples: Rain pounded on the roof all night.
He pounded the nail into the board.
Waves pound the shore during a storm.

easy.def: To make water flow out of something.
examples: Pour the milk into the cup.
I pour water on the plant.
She poured the juice.

more.def: To tip a container so that a liquid flows out.
examples: Dad poured the batter into the pan.
Rain began to pour down all at once.
He poured water from the pitcher into each glass.

easy.def: Very tiny bits of something dry.
examples: The powder is soft.
I put powder on.
Flour is a powder.

more.def: A dry material made of very tiny pieces, like dust.
examples: Flour is a white powder.
The chalk crumbled into powder.
She put a spoonful of cocoa powder in the milk.

easy.def: The strength to make things happen.
examples: The wave had great power.
I used all my power to push.
Superheroes have special powers.

more.def: The ability or strength to do something or to make something happen.
examples: A hurricane has enough power to knock down trees.
Whales have great power in their tails.
The king had the power to make new laws.

easy.def: Energy that makes machines work.
examples: The storm cut the power to our street.
Solar panels make power from sunlight.
We lost power, so I used a flashlight.

more.def: Energy, especially electricity, that is used to run machines and light buildings.
examples: The power went out in the whole city during the storm.
Windmills turn wind into power for homes.
A small battery gives power to the toy car.

easy.def: Very strong.
examples: A powerful engine.
The wind was powerful.
He is a powerful swimmer.

more.def: Having great power or strength.
examples: The powerful engine lifted the rocket.
A powerful storm knocked down trees.
The king was a powerful ruler.
